candidate_relations.reason: Optic neuropathy is a different afferent diagnosis; the phenotype is a retinal dystrophy with pathognomonic ERG, not optic-nerve disease.
Pseudotumor cerebri is a different intracranial-pressure disorder, not enhanced S-cone syndrome.
Cone-rod dystrophy is a related inherited retinal dystrophy with incompatible photoreceptor pattern versus enhanced S-cone syndrome.
Retinal detachment is a different mechanical retinal disease.
Choroidal dystrophy is a broad outer-retina/choroid category and is not ESCS.
Retinal dystrophy is the parent of enhanced S-cone syndrome but omits that specific NR2E3-related diagnosis.
Congenital stationary night blindness is a related lifelong nyctalopia but an incompatible ERG entity versus enhanced S-cone syndrome (large slow photopic/scotopic responses, flat rod ERG).
Stargardt disease is a different macular dystrophy, not ESCS.
Choroideremia is a different choroidal dystrophy.
Gyrate atrophy is a different metabolic chorioretinal atrophy.
Retinitis pigmentosa is a related inherited retinal degeneration; the fundus lacked pigmentary degeneration, conflicting with typical RP versus ESCS.
Retinal degeneration is a broad parent and omits enhanced S-cone syndrome.
Leber congenital amaurosis is a different severe infantile retinal dystrophy; acuity is 20/25–20/30.
Best vitelliform macular dystrophy is a different macular dystrophy.
Macular dystrophy is a related outer-retina category and is not ESCS.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate names enhanced S-cone syndrome; ERG with large slow photopic/scotopic responses and a flat rod ERG is characteristic.
